# 114 engine-boundary qualification handoff

This handoff is for the packaged candidate and `RRC-Golden-Companion` in Factorio 2.0 and 2.1. There is no
Factorio installation on `legalcopilot-dev`; the offline lane is therefore `IMPLEMENTED`, not `QUALIFIED`.
Milestone E is complete only after the commands below produce observations in a real game.

## Pinned independent controls

The controls below are hand-built blueprint bytes. They are literal inputs, not output from the candidate under
test and not generated by the perimeter adapter.

| control | blueprint string | independent expected rates |
|---|---|---|
| item conversion | `` | `item/iron-gear-wheel >= 1/s`; input conservation `item/iron-plate = 2/s` |
| fluid-to-item conversion | `` | `item/sulfur >= 2/s`; inputs `fluid/water = 30/s` and `fluid/petroleum-gas = 30/s` |
| non-normal-quality transfer | `` | `item-quality:10:iron-plate9:legendary >= 1/s`; normal and legendary are separate keys |

The item and fluid rates are derived from their recipes independently of the generated factory. The quality
control injects one legendary iron plate per second through the perimeter and drains one legendary iron plate per
second. A missing recipe, an internal disconnection, or a wrong quality must fail the control comparator; none may
be converted into a product-regression verdict.

## Scenario cases and limits

- `QS1`: inject `item/iron-plate`, `quality=legendary`; the accepted key must be
  `item-quality:10:iron-plate9:legendary` and every inserted stack must retain `quality=legendary`.
- `QD1`: drain one rare and one legendary iron plate. The two keys must each report one item; a combined
  `item/iron-plate` total is a failure.
- `QC1`: include the incident endpoint at `600 item/s`, not only the ordinary `120 item/s` endpoints. The
  perimeter inserter stack override is derived from the requested rate; measured rate must meet the declaration
  with positive headroom, and the dedicated perimeter pole must be separate from the factory pole.
- `QP1`: leave a deliberately unpowered generated consumer disconnected. Perimeter fixture power must not turn it
  into a powered consumer.

Use `warm_up_ticks=600` (10 seconds) and `sampling_window_ticks=1800` (30 seconds) for the game controls. The
offline adapter tests use shorter windows only to stay cheap. Compare each output and each quality independently;
the discrete-count tolerance is `max(1 item, 0.02 * expected_count)` and the rate check is a lower bound after
that tolerance. Use `timeout_seconds=120` per run, with a host command timeout of 180 seconds. A generation timeout
is `RRC_FACTORY_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`; setup, placement and capacity failures use the harness verdict and their own
`RRC_HARNESS_*` code.

Every observation must contain `prepared_input_sha256`, `config_sha256`, and `harness_qualification_id` before it
is written. Pass the prepared-input digest in the submitted case when the input file has formatting that cannot be
reproduced in the console; it is part of the submitted input, not a field added after the run. The host receipt
recomputes the digest from the named file.

## Exact game and host commands

Build and install the matching packaged candidate and companion. In a save with the required technologies, capture
the real prepared input first:

```text
/c helpers.write_file("rrc-engine-capture/<sheet-id>.txt", remote.call("rrc-engine-test", "export", "<sheet-id>"), false)
```

On the host, review the export and write the case setup:

```sh
tests/golden/add_case <case-id> --export rrc-engine-capture/<sheet-id>.txt --options <options.json>
sha256sum tests/golden/cases/<case-id>/prepared_input.json
```

Paste the reviewed table into the game console. `<prepared-input>` is the decoded capture, and
`<prepared-input-sha256>` is the hash printed by the preceding command:

```text
/c remote.call("rrc-golden-companion", "run", {case_id="<case-id>", expected_candidate_sha="<candidate-sha>", sheet_id="<sheet-id>", prepared_input=<prepared-input>, prepared_input_sha256="<prepared-input-sha256>", setup=<reviewed-setup>, engine_scenario=<reviewed-engine-scenario>})
```

Wait for both the printed terminal line and the file
`script-output/rrc-engine-evidence/<case-id>.observation.json`. Inspect `outcome_kind`, `verdict`, `rejection`
codes, quality-keyed `production.rates`, `production.warm_up`, `production.window`, and `production.timings`.
Do not call a harness failure a product regression. Re-run after fixing only the harness condition; a generated
factory failure remains a separate `factory_failure` verdict.

Copy the exact packaged archive used by the game run back to the host and file the receipt:

```sh
python3 tools/evidence_receipt.py <case-id>.observation.json <candidate.zip> \
  --case <case-id> --candidate <candidate-sha> \
  --prepared-input tests/golden/cases/<case-id>/prepared_input.json \
  --config <config.json> --output <case-id>.receipt.json
```

The receipt command must succeed with the same bytes and configuration submitted to the game. The offline focused
pass and the Lua rows do not promote this handoff to qualified; only the real Factorio runs above do that.
